reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses the general desirability of low density, strength, and corrosion resistance in HEAs, but provides no specific support for the mechanistic premises linking configurational entropy to lattice distortion, oxide film formation, or the synergistic property effects. premises: High configurational entropy suppresses phase separation and maintains a single-phase structure in lightweight HEAs.
Severe lattice distortions in a homogeneous HEA enhance mechanical strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Severe lattice distortions promote the in situ formation of coherent, protective oxide films that improve corrosion and oxidation resistance.
Loss of homogeneity (phase separation or intermetallic precipitation) degrades the synergistic strength–corrosion–oxidation performance.
